question: On 11 October 2024, China increased tariffs on European brandy by 34 %, significantly affecting products such as Brandy de Jerez, produced using the traditional criaderas y soleras method, which is unique in the world. This method is key to safeguarding the quality and reputation of the product.

Regulation 787/2019 allows derogations to protect this type of unique production system, but the Commission has yet to adopt a delegated act allowing information on average ageing to be included in the labelling of Brandy de Jerez.

Without this regulation, consumers cannot be properly informed about the product, leaving it less protected on the market and hampering its ability to compete in the face of adverse trade measures such as those imposed by China.

With the deadline for adopting delegated acts expiring in 2026, the Commission should adopt measures to increase the protection of Brandy de Jerez as a Protected Geographical Indication and to protect its traditional production method from any attempt at usurpation. In light of the above: 1.
Why has the Commission not adopted the delegated act necessary to ensure the protection of Brandy de Jerez?
If it does intend to do so, when might this be?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.1.2025) As explained in the reply to question E-002565/2024, after the entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2019/7871, the Commission considered the preparation of a delegated act laying down derogations from the youngest component rule along with appropriate control mechanisms for Brandy de Jerez.

However, certain Member States were against such proposal, considering that making an exception for one single product would weaken the very authority of the general age labelling rule, applied worldwide for many years.

In view of such disagreement, the Commission has not presented a draft for discussion to the expert group for spirit drinks and will not be in a position to do so until there is a sufficient consensus to adopt such a delegated act.

As for the deadline for adopting delegated acts expiring in May 2026, the Honourable Member is reminded that Article 46(2) of Regulation (EU) 2019/787 provides for the tacit extension of that delegation of power for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.
